title: Jacques Vallee's retrograde orbiting object at the Paris Observatory

tellings.quote: One night on July 11th, 1961, he and his colleagues noticed something truly bizarre. An unidentified object orbiting the Earth.

Vallee pointed out in a later interview, "Later, I found out that other observatories had made exactly the same observation, and that in fact American tracking stations had photographed the same thing and couldn't identify it either. It was as bright as the star Sirius. You couldn't miss it. It didn't reappear in successive weeks.
tellings.difference: Adds that other observatories and US tracking stations recorded the object, that it was as bright as Sirius, and that it did not reappear.
tellings.link_reason: The same mystery orbiting object Vallee saw in telling 3, now with corroboration from other observatories and US tracking stations.

as_told.title: Vallee's orbital mystery object seen by multiple observatories and US tracking stations

related.note: Offers the CIA Corona spy satellites as the explanation for the same orbiting object in telling 3, which is a different core claim about what the light was.

plain: On July 11, 1961, a researcher named Jacques Vallée and his colleagues at the Paris Observatory saw an unidentified object circling the Earth, moving against the direction satellites usually go. Michels tells the story and quotes a later interview in which Vallée said other observatories "had made exactly the same observation", that American tracking stations "photographed the same thing and couldn't identify it either", and that "it was as bright as the star Sirius" but "didn't reappear in successive weeks." If true, something unknown was in orbit only a few years after the first satellites.
